svg.text: The life of one exam — nothing disappears
From the front office to the gradebook. Clock and cost from the reference batch: 8 exams, 43.9 s wall clock, $0.31275 — 5.0 s and $0.0391 per exam (e2e-2026-08-19).
Cloud Run — the delivery becomes a job
the object path alone yields job id, class, subject and rubric — no batch.json needed
claim dedup + checkpoint gate: 8 upload notifications produced exactly 1 job
settler waits for uploads to stop arriving (5 s rounds, up to 6) before grading starts
2 · THE PIPELINE — ONE PUSH REQUEST, SEVEN CHECKPOINTED STAGES, ACK ONLY ON SUCCESS

g.text: one call per exam, in parallel
or hold it with a card
only on a real gain against
grade — 28.1 s of the 40.2 s of stage time, all 8 exams graded in parallel

svg.text: Stage spans total 40.2 s; the remaining 3.7 s of the 43.9 s wall clock is Firestore writing a checkpoint between every stage — which is what makes the pipeline resumable.
3 · HOW IT ENDS — THE FORK AT SYNC, AND THE THREE VISIBLE TERMINAL STATES

g.text: · at least one cited evidence span
· the student is in the manifest
· no injection found on the page

svg.text: every rule passes → write · any fails → hold

g.text: · written instructions addressed to the grader
· the grade doesn’t quote anything from the page
· the grading wasn’t sure about this one
· held as a precaution with the whole batch

svg.text: in the gradebook minutes after the scan
landed; the student can read the feedback
Measured on the deployed 16-exam demo batch
triggered by the upload alone — no HTTP call was made by hand
a card in the review queue, holding the
scanned page, the quoted evidence, the

also a card: “this exam could not be
the page — minutes or days later

g.text: She sees the page, the highlighted quote and
the reason. She never sees a job id, a stage,
a confidence number or a model name.
or send it back with no grade.
Exams held only by the batch rule are
the server refuses to bulk-release any exam
that carries a reason of its own.

svg.text: the proposed record is written unchanged → ① in the gradebook
her corrected per-criterion marks are written → ① in the gradebook
taken back: no grade is recorded, and the card is closed
the failure card stays until she grades that one exam herself
every decision writes a durable label: her choice, the proposal it replaced, the prompt version, the timestamp

Every submission in the batch manifest ends in exactly one of ① synced, ② quarantined with a card, or ③ failed with a card; the accounting denominator is the roster, so a batch cannot shrink its own numerator.
A person touches an exam in exactly two places — dropping the scans, and deciding a card. Everything in between runs unattended.
